passages.text: This is the text of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders among the exiles and to the priests, the prophets, and all the others Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet.
He lived in Jerusalem.
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar took many people from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Some elders, priests, prophets, and other people were taken into exile.
Some of these people survived in Babylon.
Jeremiah wrote a letter.
He sent this letter from Jerusalem.
He sent it to the surviving elders among the exiles.
He sent it to the priests.
He sent it to the prophets.
He sent it to all the other people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This is the text of that letter.
passages.original: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלַ֛ח יִרְמְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא מִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אֶל־ יֶ֜תֶר זִקְנֵ֣י הַגּוֹלָ֗ה וְאֶל־ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְאֶל־ הַנְּבִיאִים֙ וְאֶל־ כָּל־ הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶגְלָ֧ה נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֛ר מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

passages.text: (This was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalsmiths had been exiled from Jerusalem.)
passages.sermon:
King Jeconiah was the king of Judah.
The queen mother was his mother.
The court officials served in the king’s court.
The officials of Judah and Jerusalem were leaders in the land and city.
The craftsmen worked with their hands.
The metalsmiths shaped and worked with metal.
All these people lived in Jerusalem.
Nebuchadnezzar exiled them from Jerusalem.
They left Jerusalem and went into exile.
This happened after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalsmiths were taken from Jerusalem.
passages.original: אַחֲרֵ֣י צֵ֣את יְכָנְיָֽה־ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ וְהַגְּבִירָ֨ה וְהַסָּרִיסִ֜ים שָׂרֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֧ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְהֶחָרָ֥שׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּ֖ר מִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: The letter was entrusted to Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to King Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon. It stated: This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles who were carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon: “Build houses and settle down. Plant gardens and eat their produce.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet in Jerusalem.
He wrote a letter to the exiles in Babylon.
He gave the letter to Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah.
Zedekiah was the king of Judah.
Zedekiah sent Elasah and Gemariah to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar had taken people from Jerusalem to Babylon.
The letter said, “This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles I carried from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Build houses.
Live in them.
Plant gardens.
Eat the fruit from the gardens.”
passages.original: בְּיַד֙ אֶלְעָשָׂ֣ה בֶן־ שָׁפָ֔ן וּגְמַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־ חִלְקִיָּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֜ח צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶל־ נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֛ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל בָּבֶ֥לָה לֵאמֹֽר׃ס כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְכָל־ הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ הִגְלֵ֥יתִי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃ בְּנ֥וּ בָתִּ֖ים וְשֵׁ֑בוּ וְנִטְע֣וּ גַנּ֔וֹת וְאִכְל֖וּ אֶת־ פִּרְיָֽן׃

passages.text: Take wives and have sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they too may have sons and daughters. Multiply there; do not decrease.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the exiles in Babylon.
He told them to take wives.
He told them to have sons and daughters.
He told them to find wives for their sons.
He told them to give their daughters in marriage.
Their sons and daughters would also have children.
God told them to increase in number there.
He told them not to become fewer.
passages.original: קְח֣וּ נָשִׁ֗ים וְהוֹלִידוּ֮ בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנוֹת֒ וּקְח֨וּ לִבְנֵיכֶ֜ם נָשִׁ֗ים וְאֶת־ בְּנֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ תְּנ֣וּ לַֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְתֵלַ֖דְנָה בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנ֑וֹת וּרְבוּ־ שָׁ֖ם וְאַל־ תִּמְעָֽטוּ׃

passages.text: Seek the prosperity of the city to which I have sent you as exiles. Pray to the LORD on its behalf, for if it prospers, you too will prosper.”
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD of Hosts and the God of Israel.
God sent the people of Judah from Jerusalem to Babylon as exiles.
God commands the exiles to seek the prosperity of the city where they now live.
God tells them to pray to Him for the city.
If the city prospers, the exiles will also prosper.
passages.original: וְדִרְשׁ֞וּ אֶת־ שְׁל֣וֹם הָעִ֗יר אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִגְלֵ֤יתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ שָׁ֔מָּה וְהִתְפַּֽלְל֥וּ בַעֲדָ֖הּ אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֣י בִשְׁלוֹמָ֔הּ יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם שָׁלֽוֹם׃פ

passages.text: For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Do not be deceived by the prophets and diviners among you, and do not listen to the dreams you elicit from them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD of Hosts speaks these words.
Do not let your prophets deceive you.
These prophets live among you.
Do not let your diviners deceive you.
These diviners are also among you.
Do not listen to your dreams.
You cause yourselves to dream these dreams.
passages.original: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַל־ יַשִּׁ֧יאוּ לָכֶ֛ם נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֖ם וְקֹֽסְמֵיכֶ֑ם וְאַֽל־ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־ חֲלֹמֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם מַחְלְמִֽים׃

passages.text: For they are falsely prophesying to you in My name; I have not sent them, declares the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Some people claim to speak for the LORD.
These people say they are prophets.
They say they speak in the LORD’s name.
They are not telling the truth.
They give you false prophecies.
The LORD did not send them.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: כִּ֣י בְשֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֛ם נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֖ם בִּשְׁמִ֑י לֹ֥א שְׁלַחְתִּ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: “When Babylon’s seventy years are complete, I will attend to you and confirm My promise to restore you to this place.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says this to His people in exile.
Babylon will rule for seventy years.
After seventy years, that time will end.
Then the LORD will come to His people.
The LORD will keep His good promise.
The LORD will bring His people back.
The LORD will restore them to their land.
The LORD will return them to this place.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֠י לְפִ֞י מְלֹ֧את לְבָבֶ֛ל שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה אֶפְקֹ֣ד אֶתְכֶ֑ם וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ אֶת־ דְּבָרִ֣י הַטּ֔וֹב לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֶל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For I know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD knows His own thoughts and plans.
The LORD has plans for His people.
The LORD’s plans are for peace.
The LORD’s plans are not for harm.
The LORD will give His people a future.
The LORD will give His people hope.
passages.original: כִּי֩ אָנֹכִ֨י יָדַ֜עְתִּי אֶת־ הַמַּחֲשָׁבֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י חֹשֵׁ֥ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה מַחְשְׁב֤וֹת שָׁלוֹם֙ וְלֹ֣א לְרָעָ֔ה לָתֵ֥ת לָכֶ֖ם אַחֲרִ֥ית וְתִקְוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then you will call upon Me and come and pray to Me, and I will listen to you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people in exile.
You will call to Me.
You will come to Me.
You will pray to Me.
I will listen to you.
passages.original: וּקְרָאתֶ֤ם אֹתִי֙ וַֽהֲלַכְתֶּ֔ם וְהִתְפַּלַּלְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָ֑י וְשָׁמַעְתִּ֖י אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people in exile.
The LORD says, "You will look for Me."
You will search for Me with all your heart.
You will find Me when you seek Me this way.
passages.original: וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י וּמְצָאתֶ֑ם כִּ֥י תִדְרְשֻׁ֖נִי בְּכָל־ לְבַבְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: I will be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore you from captivity and gather you from all the nations and places to which I have banished you, declares the LORD. I will restore you to the place from which I sent you into exile.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people in exile.
The LORD says, “You will find Me.
I will let you find Me.
I will restore you from captivity.
I have scattered you among many nations.
I have sent you to many places.
I will gather you from all those nations.
I will bring you back from all those places.
I will bring you back to your own land.
I sent you away from that land.
I will restore you to the place from which I sent you into exile.
This is what the LORD declares.”
passages.original: וְנִמְצֵ֣אתִי לָכֶם֮ נְאֻם־ יְהוָה֒ וְשַׁבְתִּ֣י אֶת־ שְׁבִיתְכֶם וְקִבַּצְתִּ֣י אֶ֠תְכֶם מִֽכָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֞ם וּמִכָּל־ הַמְּקוֹמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִדַּ֧חְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֛ם שָׁ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֶל־ הַ֨מָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ הִגְלֵ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִשָּֽׁם׃

passages.text: Because you may say, “The LORD has raised up for us prophets in Babylon,” this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David’s throne and all the people who remain in this city, your brothers who did not go with you into exile— this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “I will send against them sword and famine and plague, and I will make them like rotten figs, so bad they cannot be eaten.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking to the exiles from Jerusalem who are now in Babylon.
You may say, “The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon.”
The LORD speaks about the king who sits on David’s throne.
The LORD speaks about all the people who remain in Jerusalem.
These people are your brothers who did not go with you into exile.
The LORD of Hosts says this:
I will send the sword against them.
I will send famine against them.
I will send plague against them.
I will make them like rotten figs.
These figs are so bad that no one can eat them.
passages.original: כִּ֖י אֲמַרְתֶּ֑ם הֵקִ֨ים לָ֧נוּ יְהוָ֛ה נְבִאִ֖ים בָּבֶֽלָה׃ס כִּי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ אֶל־ כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֔ד וְאֶל־ כָּל־ הָעָ֔ם הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את אֲחֵיכֶ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ יָצְא֥וּ אִתְּכֶ֖ם בַּגּוֹלָֽה׃ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִי֙ מְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ בָּ֔ם אֶת־ הַחֶ֖רֶב אֶת־ הָרָעָ֣ב וְאֶת־ הַדָּ֑בֶר וְנָתַתִּ֣י אוֹתָ֗ם כַּתְּאֵנִים֙ הַשֹּׁ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹֽעַ׃

passages.text: I will pursue them with sword and famine and plague. I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth—a curse, a desolation, and an object of scorn and reproach among all the nations to which I banish them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about those He has banished among the nations.
The LORD says, "I will pursue them."
I will use the sword against them.
I will send famine against them.
I will send plague against them.
I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
They will become a curse among the nations.
They will become a desolation among the nations.
They will become an object of scorn among the nations.
They will become a reproach among the nations.
I will do this in every nation where I have banished them.
passages.original: וְרָֽדַפְתִּי֙ אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר וּנְתַתִּ֨ים לִזְוָעָה לְכֹ֣ל׀ מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֗רֶץ לְאָלָ֤ה וּלְשַׁמָּה֙ וְלִשְׁרֵקָ֣ה וּלְחֶרְפָּ֔ה בְּכָל־ הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־ הִדַּחְתִּ֥ים שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: I will do this because they have not listened to My words, declares the LORD, which I sent to them again and again through My servants the prophets. And neither have you exiles listened, declares the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD sent His words to the people.
The LORD used His servants, the prophets, to deliver His words.
The LORD sent the prophets again and again.
The people did not listen to the LORD’s words.
The exiles also did not listen to the LORD.
The LORD declares these things.
passages.original: תַּ֛חַת אֲשֶֽׁר־ לֹא־ שָׁמְע֥וּ אֶל־ דְּבָרַ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־ עֲבָדַ֤י הַנְּבִאִים֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְשָׁלֹ֔חַ וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the exiles.
The LORD sent these people away from Jerusalem.
The LORD sent them to Babylon.
The LORD commands all these exiles to listen to His word.
The LORD says, "Hear My word, all you exiles I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon."
passages.original: וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֑ה כָּל־ הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ שִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying to you lies in My name: “I will deliver them to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them before your very eyes.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah.
Ahab and Zedekiah prophesy lies to you.
They claim to speak in the LORD’s name.
The LORD will give Ahab and Zedekiah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar will kill Ahab and Zedekiah.
He will do this in front of your eyes.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל־ אַחְאָ֤ב בֶּן־ קֽוֹלָיָה֙ וְאֶל־ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־ מַֽעֲשֵׂיָ֔ה הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֛ם בִּשְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑קֶר הִנְנִ֣י׀ נֹתֵ֣ן אֹתָ֗ם בְּיַד֙ נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֔ל וְהִכָּ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Because of them, all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon will use this curse: ‘May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire!’
passages.sermon:
All the exiles from Judah now live in Babylon.
They will use a curse because of Zedekiah and Ahab.
The exiles will say this curse to others.
They will say, “May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab.”
The king of Babylon burned Zedekiah and Ahab in the fire.
passages.original: וְלֻקַּ֤ח מֵהֶם֙ קְלָלָ֔ה לְכֹל֙ גָּל֣וּת יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבָבֶ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר יְשִֽׂמְךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ כְּצִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ וּכְאֶחָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־ קָלָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: For they have committed an outrage in Israel by committing adultery with the wives of their neighbors and speaking lies in My name, which I did not command them to do. I am He who knows, and I am a witness, declares the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah are false prophets in Israel.
They have done a terrible thing among the people of Israel.
They committed adultery with the wives of their neighbors.
They spoke lies using My name.
I did not command them to speak these lies.
I, the LORD, know what they have done.
I am a witness to their actions, says the LORD.
passages.original: יַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ עָשׂ֨וּ נְבָלָ֜ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיְנַֽאֲפוּ֙ אֶת־ נְשֵׁ֣י רֵֽעֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ דָבָ֤ר בִּשְׁמִי֙ שֶׁ֔קֶר אֲשֶׁ֖ר ל֣וֹא צִוִּיתִ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֛י הוּיֹדֵעַ וָעֵ֖ד נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: You are to tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite that this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “In your own name you have sent out letters to all the people of Jerusalem, to the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and to all the priests. You said to Zephaniah: ‘The LORD has appointed you priest in place of Jehoiada, to be the chief officer in the house of the LORD, responsible for any madman who acts like a prophet—you must put him in stocks and neck irons.
passages.sermon:
Shemaiah was a man from Nehelam.
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God is the God of Israel.
God told someone to speak to Shemaiah.
God said this to Shemaiah.
Shemaiah, you sent letters in your own name.
You sent these letters to all the people in Jerusalem.
You sent these letters to Zephaniah, the son of Maaseiah, who is a priest.
You sent these letters to all the priests.
You said to Zephaniah:
The LORD has made you priest instead of Jehoiada the priest.
You are to be the chief officer in the house of the LORD.
You are responsible for every person who acts like a madman or claims to be a prophet.
You must put such a person in stocks and neck irons.
passages.original: וְאֶל־ שְׁמַעְיָ֥הוּ הַנֶּחֱלָמִ֖י תֹּאמַ֥ר לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר יַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּה֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתָּ בְשִׁמְכָ֜ה סְפָרִ֗ים אֶל־ כָּל־ הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְאֶל־ צְפַנְיָ֤ה בֶן־ מַֽעֲשֵׂיָה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֶ֥ל כָּל־ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃ יְהוָ֞ה נְתָנְךָ֣ כֹהֵ֗ן תַּ֚חַת יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵ֔ן לִֽהְי֤וֹת פְּקִדִים֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה לְכָל־ אִ֥ישׁ מְשֻׁגָּ֖ע וּמִתְנַבֵּ֑א וְנָתַתָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֶל־ הַמַּהְפֶּ֖כֶת וְאֶל־ הַצִּינֹֽק׃

passages.text: So now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who poses as a prophet among you?
passages.sermon:
Shemaiah the Nehelamite spoke to Zephaniah the priest.
Shemaiah asked Zephaniah a question.
Jeremiah is from Anathoth.
Jeremiah claims to be a prophet among the people.
Shemaiah asked Zephaniah, “Why have you not rebuked Jeremiah?”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה לָ֚מָּה לֹ֣א גָעַ֔רְתָּ בְּיִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָֽעֲנְּתֹתִ֑י הַמִּתְנַבֵּ֖א לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: For he has sent to us in Babylon, claiming: Since the exile will be lengthy, build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat their produce.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet from Anathoth.
He sent a message to the people in Babylon.
He said the exile will last a long time.
He told the people to build houses.
He told them to settle down in those houses.
He told them to plant gardens.
He told them to eat the fruit from those gardens.
passages.original: כִּ֣י עַל־ כֵּ֞ן שָׁלַ֥ח אֵלֵ֛ינוּ בָּבֶ֥ל לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲרֻכָּ֣ה הִ֑יא בְּנ֤וּ בָתִּים֙ וְשֵׁ֔בוּ וְנִטְע֣וּ גַנּ֔וֹת וְאִכְל֖וּ אֶת־ פְּרִיהֶֽן׃

passages.text: (Zephaniah the priest, however, had read this letter to Jeremiah the prophet.)
passages.sermon:
Zephaniah was a priest.
Zephaniah read this letter aloud.
Jeremiah was a prophet.
Zephaniah read the letter to Jeremiah.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֛א צְפַנְיָ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת־ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה בְּאָזְנֵ֖י יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah: “Send a message telling all the exiles what the LORD says concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite. Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you—though I did not send him—and has made you trust in a lie, this is what the LORD says: ‘I will surely punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one left among this people, nor will he see the good that I will bring to My people, declares the LORD, for he has preached rebellion against the LORD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message.
The LORD told Jeremiah to send this message to all the exiles.
The LORD spoke about Shemaiah the Nehelamite.
Shemaiah the Nehelamite claimed to be a prophet.
Shemaiah prophesied to the exiles.
The LORD did not send Shemaiah.
Shemaiah made the people trust in a lie.
The LORD said He would punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite.
The LORD said He would punish Shemaiah’s descendants.
No one from Shemaiah’s family would remain among the people.
Shemaiah would not see the good that the LORD would do for His people.
The LORD declared this.
Shemaiah spoke rebellion against the LORD.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃ שְׁלַ֤ח עַל־ כָּל־ הַגּוֹלָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ שְׁמַעְיָ֖ה הַנֶּחֱלָמִ֑י יַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ נִבָּ֨א לָכֶ֜ם שְׁמַעְיָ֗ה וַֽאֲנִי֙ לֹ֣א שְׁלַחְתִּ֔יו וַיַּבְטַ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל־ שָֽׁקֶר׃ לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִ֨י פֹקֵ֜ד עַל־ שְׁמַעְיָ֣ה הַנֶּחֱלָמִי֮ וְעַל־ זַרְעוֹ֒ לֹא־ יִהְיֶ֨ה ל֜וֹ אִ֣ישׁ׀ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב׀ בְּתוֹךְ־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה וְלֹֽא־ יִרְאֶ֥ה בַטּ֛וֹב אֲשֶׁר־ אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶֽׂה־ לְעַמִּ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־ סָרָ֥ה דִבֶּ֖ר עַל־ יְהוָֽה׃ס
